title: Patience and Faith
english: The wrath of God is almost upon us, trampling and slaughtering the strong and the fat like rams and bulls.
To the wealthy it is said: Come now, weep and wail over the troubles that are coming upon you.
You have lived in luxury, squandered your wealth on the earth, and nourished your hearts as if it were a day of slaughter.
The leaders of the Jews have become like those who graze in a fertile and spacious land, feeding on the donations from the people.
Having been caught as if by the Lord’s sword, the cowards are urged: therefore, brothers, be patient until the coming of the Lord.
For if God delays the punishment of sinners, waiting for their repentance, He does not do so because He has changed or because He loves sinners, but because He gives them time to return.
Having declared the punishment of the wicked, He advises those who have been wronged to be patient, awaiting the coming of the Lord.

At the same time, He also forbids taking oaths and encourages diligence in prayer and psalm-singing, and having faith in the priests of God and love towards each other, as also to pray for one another.
The proof of the power of prayer is brought forward in the example of Elijah.
And finally, the reward of sinners who return.
But above all, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven nor by earth nor by any other oath.
If someone shameless, not entreating your life, dares to impose an oath on you, let your yes be yes and your no be no, instead of an oath.
This is because swearing by heaven and earth risks giving creation honor above itself, which is to make it godlike.
For those who swear by something greater are, in effect, swearing by that greater thing, as the Apostle says.
If you believe in the one you do not see, you rejoice with inexpressible and glorified joy, obtaining the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls (1 Peter 1:8-9).
How terrible and difficult is unbelief, but how great is faith as a good, a precursor to every salvation.
As it is written: Behold, I place a chosen, precious stone in Zion, and the one who believes in it will not be put to shame (Isaiah 28:16).
Therefore the honor is yours, to those who believe.
This stone is the Lord Jesus Christ, who is called chosen, precious, and honorable, reflecting the glory and excellence of divinity.
He is also called a cornerstone, as He unites the two peoples, from Israel and from the nations, into one spiritual temple through one faith.
And the one who believes in Him will not be put to shame.
But observe how He brings relief to the afflicted…
The text breaks off here, leaving the sentence incomplete.

title: The Power of the Tongue
english: The chosen stone is placed in the foundations of Zion, and what is the benefit from this? The one believing in him will not be put to shame, because it is essential to control one's tongue, stopping it from evil, as the Bible says that death and life are in the hand of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21). Those who can control their tongue will eat its fruits, and this restraint is a great virtue, just as not having it is a painful disease. The restraint of the tongue is a crucial aspect of being a perfect person, able to bridle also the whole body, as Scripture says that if someone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body (James 3:2).

The Only-Begotten, with authority, cried out to the souls who suffered similarly, according to the plan of the economy, saying to those in bonds, 'Come out', and to those in darkness, 'Be revealed'. This was his proclamation to those in Hades, that he might free those who were about to believe, if he had come in the flesh at the time of their life, if the incarnation was indeed profitable. For these also certainly recognized him in Hades, whom the gatekeepers of Hades, upon seeing him, were terrified by, and the bronze gates were broken, and the iron bars were shattered.

For the things beyond our economy are beyond nature and tradition, and just as Christ cried out equally to all on earth through his bodily presence, and those who believed were helped, so also through his descent into Hades, he freed those who believed and recognized him from the bonds of death. The souls of those who lived in idolatry and lawless debauchery were unable to see the rays of the divine appearance, and thus they could not faithfully recognize the one who came to free all, who appeared to those below and proclaimed to all in common, showing both his philanthropic and just nature.

title: Faith and Hospitality
english: When we abandon the Creator and God of all, we inevitably serve demonic and misanthropic beings, and live as friends to them.
Christ suffered in the flesh for us, and we should arm ourselves with the same mindset as he did.
The Word of God became flesh and suffered voluntarily, showing us that true strength comes from God.
As we are baptized into Christ's death, we become one with him, impassible in divinity but passible in flesh.
Christ is God, and as such, he is impassible in his divinity, but passible in his flesh.
When we receive brothers at table, we should not be anxious about much service, but rather focus on the encounters with our guests, and gain the reward of hospitality.
In what seems difficult, we should show what is noble.
We did not follow clever myths when we made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, but rather we became eyewitnesses of his greatness.
For he received honor and glory from God the Father, and a voice was brought to him by the magnificent foot of glory.

The problems of the heretics are indeed myths and human wisdom, which Paul writes to us to avoid, as he says, 'Avoid a heretic after a first and second warning' is not our concern, but rather Paul's warning to avoid heretics (Titus 3:10).
The heretics, not having the truth, are forced to wander in various speeches to defend the falsehood.
But we are not so, for we have seen the truth with our eyes, being with him on the mountain.
We also have the prophets who foretold this truth to us, and thus the word became more confirmed to us through sight than through the prophets.
For what they said, Christ confirmed by being present, and we are witnesses who also heard the testimony.
For not having followed clever myths, we made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, but having become eyewitnesses of his greatness.
We should not consider it a strange occurrence to us to face narrowness and tribulations and bodily infirmities, but rather show what is noble in such situations.
